subject: maths
title: Pie Charts
welcome_lead: Pie charts split a full 360° circle by frequency. Each slice shows a category's share.
meta_desc: Draw and read pie charts in this KS3 data handling adventure.
final_note: Brilliant! Pie charts are sliced clearly for you now.

concepts.def: Circular chart split into sectors by proportion.
Sum of all frequencies, equal to 360°.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A pie chart total is always 360°.

If total frequency is 30, angle per item = 360 ÷ 30 = 12° each.
If a category has frequency 8 and angle per item is 12°: sector angle = 8 × 12 = 96°.
If a sector is 90° in a pie chart of 60 people: that sector represents (90/360) × 60 = 15 people.

On a bar chart showing the number of pets, the bar for 'cat' has height 7. What does the 7 mean?
options: Seven cats are owned by the people in total.
Seven people (or items) in the survey chose 'cat' — frequency is the count.
Cats are the seventh most popular pet.

mcqs.q: Which average is best to use for the data set [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 100]?
options: The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
The mean — it always gives the most accurate average.
The median (3.5) — it isn't distorted by the outlier 100, unlike the mean.
15, because 15% means 15 units out of any amount.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
